item.title: Trump says Putin 'would like to make a deal' to end Ukraine war; urges him to end 'military aggression' | Key takeaways
item.description: A week after meeting Vladimir Putin in China, Donald Trump said he had urged the Russian leader to end military aggression across Europe. He also defended maintaining friendly ties with Putin, discussed a possible peace deal and said the Russian leader could attend the G20 summit in Florida.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: A week after US President Donald Trump met with his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, in China's Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, Trump on Thursday (local time) said he had asked Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe.According to reports, his remarks came a day after he hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida, following which the two leaders issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the war in Ukraine. The remarks come amid a shift in tone towards the Russian leader, whom Trump had called his friend just last week, AFP reported.The US President said he had raised the matter with Putin during their meeting in China last week, expressing hope that the request would help pave the way for an agreement to end Russia's prolonged war in Ukraine.Against this backdrop, Trump's latest remarks offer fresh insights into his approach towards Putin, the ongoing Ukraine war and the prospects of a peace deal.Here are five key takeaways from what the US President said:1. On his Truth Social platform, Trump said, "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe." He added that he did so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly."He also said he believed that bringing Putin's war in Ukraine to an end was a strong possibility. Trump did not clarify which territories he was referring to, nor did he explicitly mention Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, triggering Europe's largest conflict since World War II.2. Speaking to reporters in Florida on Thursday (local time), Trump said he did not know whether Putin would attend the G20 summit scheduled to take place next month in Florida. However, he added that the Russian leader would be welcome if he wanted to attend, Reuters reported."If he wanted to come, he certainly can," Trump said. He acknowledged that some people would not like to see the Russian leader at the December 14-15 meeting, and expressed doubt that Putin himself would want to attend. "If it were up to me, I'd like to have him," Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, where he was spending the Thanksgiving holiday.3. Trump said his Russian counterpart "would like to make a deal" to end the war in Ukraine, adding that his priority was to stop the ongoing loss of life on both sides. During a Thanksgiving call with US military personnel from his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thursday (local time), alongside First Lady Melania Trump, the US President reiterated his desire to reach an agreement with Moscow.4. When asked by a reporter about his earlier description of Putin as a friend and his subsequent comments on Russian military aggression, Trump said maintaining cordial ties with the Russian leader was important to securing a peace deal."Well, things can be said, but look, you have to understand something. We want to make a deal. We want to stop killing," he said. He added, "I could say he's not a friend or with it--well, I want to make a deal. I got to get a deal done. They're losing 25,000 people a month."Explaining his approach further, the US President said that expressing hostility towards Putin could complicate efforts to settle. He also compared it to the strained relationship between the Russian leader and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.Trump noted, "I could walk in and say, 'I don't like you,' and then we have the same problem that we have with Zelenskyy and Putin. You know, they have the biggest problem to that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other, okay?"5. Trump also referred to investigations into Russia's alleged interference in US politics, which he described as a "fake" investigation, before reiterating that his latest discussions with Putin had been positive."So when I go and happen to get along with him--I've known him a long time, don't forget he had to suffer through a fake 'Russia, Russia, Russia' investigation, which was made up and totally-- was a total con job. And he had to go through that and hear things that turned out to be totally false. So, we had a very good discussion. The bottom line is he would like to make a deal," Trump said.Trump's remarks highlighted his stated focus on negotiating an end to the Ukraine war and his willingness to maintain diplomatic engagement with Putin. However, it remains to be seen whether the Russian President will respond to Trump's latest appeal and take concrete steps towards reaching a peace agreement with Ukraine.(with agency inputs)

item.title: 'I did a great thing': Trump defends Jensen Huang's 'second term' as Nvidia CEO despite national security concerns
item.description: Trump has defended his role in Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO, calling it a “great thing” despite national security concerns. He said Huang's second stint would be even better and dismissed questions about potential security risks.
item.dc:creator: Prabhakar Jha
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has defended his decision to facilitate Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's chief executive, calling it a positive development for the country and the world.Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thursday, Trump said Huang was happy to return to the company and had described the move as his "second term".Trump said he had not spoken to Huang since Nvidia announced his reinstatement but expected to speak with him before he resumed his role. He also expressed confidence in Huang's leadership, saying the CEO would do an even better job the second time around."Everybody's replaceable, I guess, but I just thought, I saw what was happening with the company, what was happening with the stock, and I think it's a great thing that he's going back," Trump said, according to Bloomberg.Trump praises Nvidia's upcoming chipsTrump also praised Nvidia's upcoming chips, saying two new products were expected to outperform its Blackwell chip, which he described as the company's current leading technology.Asked about concerns that Huang could pose a security threat, particularly given the questions surrounding his personal associations, Trump dismissed the reservations."Based on information and belief, I think he's absolutely fine," he said. When pressed to identify the information behind his assessment, Trump replied: "The information I have, which is a lot of information."Trump added that he believed he had done "a great thing for our country and even for the world".Why has Huang's return raised national security concerns?Huang's reinstatement has drawn criticism from both Republicans and Democrats, with lawmakers raising questions about the administration's intervention and potential counterintelligence risks.According to a CBS News report, US intelligence officials briefed congressional staffers that China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) may have monitored Alice Huang, who was previously associated with Jensen Huang, and attempted to obtain information from her after she began an affair with the Nvidia CEO.The intelligence agencies have not established the full extent of the matter. They have also found no evidence so far that Alice Huang was specifically directed to collect information about Jensen Huang or shared information of substantial intelligence value with China, CBS News reported.The concerns were reportedly outlined in a classified memorandum prepared by Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio. The document, which summarised intelligence including intercepted communications, was circulated among senior administration officials.Huang is scheduled to meet House lawmakers privately on December 1 and is expected to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, Bloomberg reported.

item.title: Thanksgiving celebrations turn sour in US as storm batters East Coast; 900,000 homes without power, flights cancelled
item.description: A powerful Nor'easter battered the US on Thanksgiving, leaving nearly a million utility customers without electricity, disrupting flights and holiday travel, triggering coastal flood warnings and forcing the postponement of Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: Thanksgiving celebrations were disrupted for millions across the United States on Thursday (local time) after a powerful storm battered the country's central and eastern regions, triggering adverse weather conditions, knocking out power to nearly a million homes and businesses, and snarling holiday travel.Nearly a million without power across USAccording to PowerOutage.us data cited by Reuters, more than 961,000 US utility customers were without electricity as of 7:30 pm ET (6 am IST), as families prepared for traditional holiday gatherings. Pennsylvania was the worst-hit, with over 235,000 outages, followed by New Jersey (180,000), Maryland (156,000), Virginia (132,000), Missouri (106,000), New York (56,000) and Delaware (21,000).Flights cancelled, Thanksgiving parade postponedHeavy rain and strong winds from the "Nor'easter" created treacherous travel conditions during what is considered one of the busiest holiday periods in the US. Data from FlightAware showed that roughly 400 flights were cancelled and more than 2,000 delayed across the country, mostly in the East.According to reports, the strengthening storm had already forced the postponement of events, including the Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade, which has now been rescheduled for Saturday, marking the first time the annual procession has been delayed. The governors of New York and New Jersey declared states of emergency, warning of damaging winds, heavy rainfall and severe coastal flooding through Friday.Coastal flood warnings issued as winds intensifyAdditionally, the National Weather Service issued coastal flood warnings for several counties in New York and New Jersey, including all five boroughs of New York City. Citing AccuWeather meteorologist Alyssa Glenny, Bloomberg reported that wind gusts had reached 72 miles per hour at Stingray Point, Virginia, while coastal areas of New Jersey and Long Island were bracing for gusts of up to 80 mph as the storm moved northward. Glenny said, "We’re looking at the afternoon going into the evening for peak rainfall in New York."Flooding affected several areas along the East Coast, while inland regions also experienced disruptions. Strong winds and waterlogged ground caused trees to collapse onto power lines and residential properties.In Maryland's suburbs near the US capital, authorities urged nearly two million customers to limit their tap water consumption, citing concerns that power cuts could disrupt the water treatment system.Officials urge caution as bridges closeMeanwhile, officials urged people to restrict road travel as several major bridges were closed due to high winds. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, who declared a state of emergency on Wednesday over the adverse weather conditions, asked residents to stay safe and take precautions. In a post on X, she wrote, "Keep your devices charged, report power outages directly to your utility provider, and stay away from downed power lines."California also faces weather disruptionThe disruption along the country's East Coast came as Californians also faced weather-related difficulties this week, with massive waves battering the coast, prompting evacuations in some areas and soaking San Francisco.Trump announces disaster assistance for FloridaSeparately, US President Donald Trump issued a formal disaster declaration for Florida to release immediate funding through the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), following recent flooding and the impact of Hurricane Isaias last month. He said Florida's total combined aid would amount to nearly $100 million, adding that he would consider assisting other states affected by storms this week, if needed. The US President said, “Well, we’ll look at that; we have some requests from others. I think Florida maybe got hit the worst.”The storm's impact across several states highlighted the widespread disruption to holiday travel, power supplies, and daily life as millions of Americans marked Thanksgiving.
